lines.x: Sentry duty, yeah, I get it, that's what the F.N.G. always gets, no matter where… it's not that? Well, you say that, but I find it hard to believe that you won't need protection.

Come, open your palm face-up. That's right, here you go. Yup, I made it myself. Making filled candy is quite a bother, and this is all that I made. Maybe it's not that rare on the outside, but you should understand its worth—are you done? Good. I have something to ask you. I won't take silence for an answer.

That Sarkaz was really something. I didn't have to hold anything back, and my blade's still warm, even now… no, it's not so dangerous. It's a bad day if you rip your clothes in the training room. Yeah, ranged caster duel. What were you thinking it was?

'I'm here, Doctor.' Voice imitation Arts, a staple for any war caster. Not close enough? Check this out then, at the tip of my blade—no playing with fire in the office? It's just an Arts illusion, there's no real fire. You draw a strange line for what spooks you.

The Armies have a clear delineation. If you're not with the Second Army, you're with the Fourth. No one asks what the shashka thinks. My Sechin was one such weapon. No, what's between Evgeny and I isn't personal. It's not that complicated.

My comrades believe I'm favored by fate, toying with my prey before dragging it into hell, just the monster with long-drooped eyelids that my code name represents. But the true monster is war itself, toying with and destroying everyone, making no distinction between noble and commoner, hero and villain.

Yes, I know that ignoring orders is a major dereliction of duty, I just didn't think you, of all people, would be criticizing the mistake I made in the Far North… you want to thank me? It's not like I meant to spare those people. There's nothing to thank me for.

What does this mean? And this? And this? How do you manage to read these scribblings? They're like worms crawling on the page. I used to have someone to read stuff like this to me. Sirka could read anything like singing a song. Maybe you can too. Audiobooks? Not interested.

Brewing, sugarmaking, woodworking and smithing. We began to learn these things as soon as we learned to walk. That's all we're allowed to do to pass the time off the battlefield. Here, give it a try. Homebrews don't pass security checks; I had to smuggle this kvass in.
You managed to fall asleep while standing and reading? Kind of a shame that someone with such a gift for recuperation is not a warrior.

A hood and clothing that covers your entire body. You have a past you want to hide too? It's all right, I understand. Scioppa Razin, here to establish a partnership. You can call me 'Viy', that's what the boys call me.

Zzz… oh! Ahem. No, I wasn't sleeping. This Phidia lady can cause the enemy to drop their weapons and surrender in total silence? She's a caster too, isn't she? Very interesting. Yeah, I only saw the ending.

Seems a lot more formal than the First Army's external promotions. No need for bargaining or bribery to make sure the order doesn't get held up somewhere. Didn't think so, did you? We even worked under those pure-blood Ursines.
I thought a symbolic medal marking our cooperation was all there was to it, but now… this is awkward. I'm gonna have to repay you before this trust runs out.
Who's in charge?
Can I bring a few of my guys?
Back in battle. It hasn't been that long.
Focus!
Best put me where I can't make friendly fire.
At the ready.
Visibility's good.
Any orders?
This blade is my mother too.
It wipes away pain.
It extinguishes fear.
Who else to pray to?
Witness my promised victory.
I'm not used to this. Where are the rowdy boys pushing me to sing?
I'll stay behind and make sure there are no loose ends.
So close!
Back on a ship again.
You got lucky this time. Don't cry when strange Arts set your fingers on fire next time.
I liked that. Do it again.
Arknights.

'Mother sheds tears by the red corner, while father in his silence grows stone-cold. Sister goes barefoot into the river, that keeps children of freedom in its hold.' I used to sing to my comrades the whereabouts of my families, and now I sing for you. Ursine custom is to celebrate the seventh day of a new year, but nevertheless, Happy New Year, Doctor.
I'm bored. Let's play poker.

Blood? Oh, don't worry, just missed a spot while cleaning up. I was in a hurry to give this to you. Got the materials from Engineering, and polished the edges myself. Hang it on your belt, just like I do. Say, is it your birthday or your naming day again?

Once I thought I had to be an executioner to be free. Meeting you has reminded me that the first who fought to become free Volniki did not do it to distinguish themselves from other Ursines. We looked for another way forward, and took the long way round.
